Why it could not be computed
Where the energy lost comes from
The time group on the report
Charged to the O&M contractor by default
The time group code must be unique.
In a partial outage the machine is still generating. Whatever reached the meter must not be counted as lost.
The old figure computed by the system on the previous run has been DELETED, because this run could not rebuild it: %s
Could not be computed: %s\n\nThe old figure is left as it was — "could not be computed" is not the same as "zero".
Leave it empty and this category's hours fall into the "not grouped yet" row on the report — shown rather than disappearing.
the price is unknown — the plant has no power purchase agreement and no price declared; leaving it empty is better than multiplying by 0

Captures the price at the moment of calculation. A power purchase tariff escalates year by year, so recomputing two years later without a captured price changes the old figure with nobody aware of it.
Where the figure in the "energy lost" field came from. Kept because an outage typed in by a person and one computed by the system carry very different weight when the claim goes to the contractor.

Only a SUGGESTION when the user attributes responsibility for each outage. The real attribution still lives on each record, because the same group is sometimes the contractor's fault and sometimes not.
The hours of an ungrouped category fall into the\n "not grouped yet" row on the report — shown rather than\n disappearing, but they should still be grouped.

Declared at plant level only, and used only where there is no power purchase agreement to look up. With an agreement, the price comes from the agreement's tariff — declare a price in two places and sooner or later the two disagree.

Mark exactly ONE group. Curtailment hours are deducted when computing the operating hours used for the performance ratio — the machine was still available, the grid simply would not take it. Without the mark, the two ways of computing operating hours give the same figure, and the performance section is wrong with it.

Twenty-three standard categories folded into the few rows an operator can actually read. Stored by the standard, shown by group — wind and solar reports fold them differently, so the mapping has to be declarable.

This category counts towards the INCIDENTS section of the daily report.

The flag sits on the TIME CATEGORY rather than the reporting group, because that is where the meaning lies: the "Equipment fault" group still contains the category "PLANNED repair intervention", while the category "Forced outage — awaiting materials" sits in the "Downtime caused by the O&M contractor" group. Use the group as the measure and the incidents section is both short and padded at once.

DECLARED rather than detected by name: change one word of the name and the incidents section is empty with nothing to say so.
